G0700.def:
ἀρέσκω 
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] 
__1. to please (Hom., Hdt., al.): with dative of person(s), Matthieu 14:6, Marc 6:22, Romains 8:8 15:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:15 4:1, 1 Corinthiens 7:32-34 Galates 1:10, 2 Timothée 2:4; before ἐνώπισν (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 65. 
__2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (see M, Th., ICC, 1 Co., ll with; Cremer, 640 f.); Romains 15:1, 3, 1 Corinthiens 10:33, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:4.†

G0701.def:
ἀρεστός, -ή, -όν
(ἀρέσκω), [in LXX for יָשָׁר, etc. ;] 
pleasing, agreeable (Hdt., Xen., and later writers; see Cremer, 641 f; MM, see word): with dative of person(s), Jean 8:29, Actes 12:3; before ἐνώπιον, with genitive (Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), 1 Jean 3:22; ἀρεστόν ἐστιν, with accusative and inf (El., § 69, 5; 72, 5), Actes 6:2.†

G0702.def:
Ἀρέτας (WH, Ἀρ.; Intr., 313), -α, ὁ, 
Aretas, an Arabian king: 2 Corinthiens 11:32 (Deiss., BS, 183 f., thinks the proper spelling Ἀρέθας was changed, as Schürer suggests, "by desire to Hellenise a barbaric name by assimilation to ἀρετή").†

G0704.def:
ἀρήν, ἀρνός, ὁ
(nom, not in use, exc. in early times: see MM, see word), [in LXX for מְרִיא, כֶּבֶשׂ, etc. ;] 
a lamb: Luc 10:3.†

G0705.def:
ἀριθμέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX for סָפַר pi., פָּקַד pi., etc. ;] 
to number (esp. for payment, MM, see word): Matthieu 10:30, Luc 12:7, Apocalypse 7:9.†

G0706.def:
ἀριθμός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for מִסְפָּר ;] 
number, a number: Luc 22:3, Jean 6:10, Actes 4:4 5:36 6:7 11:21 16:5, Romains 9:27, Apocalypse 5:11 7:4 9:16 13:17-18 15:2 20:8 (for exx. of mystical use in π., see MM, see word).†

G0707.def:
Ἁριμαθεία
(WH, Ἁρ.), -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Ἁριμαθάιμ, 1 Rois 1:1, al. (רָמָה) ;] 
Arimathæa: Matthieu 27:57, Marc 15:43, Luc 23:51, Jean 19:38.†

G0708.def:
Ἀρίσταρχος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄριστος, ἀρχός; i.e. best-ruling) 
Aristarchus: Actes 19:29 20:4 27:2, Colossiens 4:10, Phm 24

G0709.def:
ἀριστάω, -ῶ
(ἄριστον), [in LXX: Genèse 43:25 (לֶחֶם אָכַל), 1 Rois 14:24 (לֶחֶם), 3Ki.13:7 (סָעַד), Tob.2:1 * ;] 
__1. prop., to breakfast: Jean 21:12, 15 
__2. In late Gk., to take a meal, dine: Luc 11:37.†

G0710.def:
ἀριστερός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX for שְׂמֹאול ;] 
left, on the left: ὅπλα, 2 Corinthiens 6:7; ἡ ἀ.. (sc. χείρ), Matthieu 6:3; ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, on the left (MM, see word ): Marc 10:37, Luc 23:33.†

G0711.def:
Ἀριστόβουλος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄριστος, βουλή, i.e. best-counselling) 
Aristobulus, a Christian: Romains 16:10.†

G0712.def:
ἄριστον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX: 3Ki.3:1 (לֶחֶם), Tob.2:1, 4, al. ;] 
__1 1, prop., breakfast. 
__2. In late Gk. = cl. δεῖτνον, dinner: Matthieu 22:4, Luc 11:38 14:12.†

G0713.def:
ἀρκετός, -ή, -όν
(ἀρκέω), [in Aq.: Deutéronome 25:2 * ;] 
sufficient: Matthieu 6:34 (on the neut., see B1., § 31, 2); before ἵνα (M, Pr., 210), Matthieu 10:25; with inf., 1 Pierre 4:3 (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 257; MM, see word).†

G0714.def:
ἀρκέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX for הוֹן, etc. ;] 
__1. to keep off; with dative, to assist. 
__2. to suffice: with dative of person(s), Jo 67, 2 Corinthiens 12:9; impers., Matthieu 25:9, Jean 14:8 (MM, see word). Pass., to be satisfied: with dative of thing(s), Luc 3:14, 1 Timothée 6:8, Hébreux 13:5; before ἐπί, III Jn 10.†

G0715.def:
ἅρκος
(Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), [in LXX for דֹּב ;] -ου, ὁ, ἡ, 
a bear: Apocalypse 13:2. (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, see word)†

G0716.def:
ἅρμα, -τος, τό
(ἀραρίσκω, to join), [in LXX רָכַב ;] 
a chariot: Actes 8:28-29, 38, Apocalypse 9:9.†

G0717.def:
Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹן), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, 2 Chroniques 35:22, Μαγεδώ, Juges 1:27; Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Apocalypse 16:16 (see Swete, in l, but also Thayer, see word).†
Ἅρ, 
indecl., Apocalypse 16:16, see, Ἁρμαγεδών 
Μαγεδών, 
Magedon: Apocalypse 16:16 (WH, Ἅρ M. for Ἁρμαγεδών, which see).†

G0718.def:
ἁρμόζω
(ἁρμός), [in LXX for אמן, etc. ;] 
__1. to fit, join. 
__2. of marriage, to betroth. Mid., 
__(a) to join to oneself, marry, take to wife; (b) to give in marriage: 2 Corinthiens 11:2 (for this there is no direct parallel. But see M, Pr., 160; MM, see word).†

G0719.def:
ἁρμός, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Sir.27:2, 4Ma.10:5 * ;] 
a joining, joint: Hébreux 4:12.†

G0720.def:
ἀρνέομαι -οῦμαι, depon., 
[in LXX: Genèse 18:15 (כָּחַשׁ pi.), Wis.12:27 16:16 17:10, 4Ma.8:7 4Mac 10:15 * ;] 
__1. to deny, say no, opposite to είπεῖν: absol., Matthieu 26:70, Luc 8:45; before ἅτι, 1 Jean 2:22; with inf., Hébreux 11:24 
__2. In late Gk. (MM, see word), with accusative of person(s), to deny, refuse to acknowledge, disown: Actes 3:14 7:35; Ἰησοῦν, Matthieu 10:33, 2 Timothée 2:12, 1 Jean 2:22, Ju 4; ἑαυτόν, Luc 9:23, 2 Timothée 2:13 (prove false to) 
__3. C. accusative of thing(s) (in cl. to refuse), to deny, abjure: 1 Timothée 5:8, Tite 2:12, 2 Timothée 3:5 (cf. ἀπαρνέομαι)

G0721.def:
ἀρνίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ἀρήν; see MM, see word), [in LXX: Psaumes 114:4, 6 (pl., צֹאן בֵּן), Jérémie 11:19 (כֶּבֶשׂ), Jérémie 50:45 (צָעִיר)* ;] 
a little lamb, a lamb: Jean 21:15, Apocalypse 2:7.†

G0722.def:
ἀροτριάω, -ῶ
(ἄροτρον), [in LXX: Deutéronome 22:10, al. (חָרַשׁ), Ésaïe 7:25 (עֲדַר) ;] 
later form of ἀρόω, to plough (MM, see word): Luc 17:7, 1 Corinthiens 9:10.†

G0723.def:
ἄροτρον, -ου, τό
(ἀρόω, to plough), [in LXX chiefly for אֵת ;] 
a plough: Luc 9:62.†

G0724.def:
ἁρπαγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἁρπάζω), [in LXX (as also ἅρπαγμα) for גָּזֵל, etc. ;] 
pillage, plundering, robbery: Matthieu 23:25, Luc 11:39, Hébreux 10:34.†

G0725.def:
ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ
(ἁρπάζω); 
__1. prop., accusative, to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., Deu Puer. Educ., p. 12A), Philippiens 2:6, AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, see word). 
__2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα (Eze.22:25, of a lion's prey, ), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phi, l.with, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, see word, esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. Romains 11:9, where cf. LXX; 1 Corinthiens 13:9, 2 Co 19), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, ll with†

G0726.def:
ἁρπάζω 
[in LXX chiefly for גָּזַל, טָרַף ;] 
to seize, catch up, snatch away, carry off by force: with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 12:29 13:19, Jean 10:12, 28-29; τ. βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, Matthieu 11:12; with accusative of person(s), Jean 6:15, Actes 8:39 23:10, Ju 23; pass., before ἕως, 2 Corinthiens 12:2; εἰς, 2 Corinthiens 12:4, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:17; πρός, Apocalypse 12:5 (cf. δι-, συν-αρπάζω, and see MM, see word).†

G0727.def:
ἅρπαξ, -αγος, ὁ, ἡ
(ἁρπάζω), [in LXX: Genèse 49:27 (טָרַף) * ;] 
rapacious: Matthieu 7:15, Luc 18:11; as subst., a swindler, an extortioner (MM, see word), 1 Corinthiens 5:10-11 6:10.†

G0728.def:
ἀρραβών
(T, ἀραβ-: 2Co, ll. with), -ώνος, ὁ, [in LXX: Genèse 38:17-20 (עֲרָבוֹן)* ;] 
an earnest, part payment in advance for security, a first instalment: 2 Corinthiens 1:22 5:5, Éphésiens 1:14. (The word is found in cl. and was prob. brought to Greece by the Phænicians (AR, Eph., l.with). It is found in π. with both spellings (see Milligan, NTD, 73). In MGr. ἀρραβῶνα is an engagement ring; see MM, see word)†

G0729.def:
ἄραφος, -ον (Rec. ἄρραφο), 
(ῥάπτω, to sew) 
without seam: Jean 19:23.†

G0730.def:
ἄρσην (ἄρρην, T, in Romains 1:27; Rec. in Apocalypse 12:5, 13) -ενος, ὁ, ἡ, ἄρσεν, τό 
(old Attic for ἄρρην, see supr.; both forms are found in π.; MM, see word), [in LXX chiefly for זָכָר ;] 
male: Matthieu 19:4, Marc 10:6, Luc 2:23, Romains 1:27, Galates 3:28, Apocalypse 12:5, 13.†

G0731.def:
ἄρρητος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., ῥητός, ῥέω), [in Sm.: Lévitique 18:23 * ;] 
__1. unspoken (Hom., al.). 
__2. unspeakable (Hat., al.; frequently in Inscr.; MM, see word): 2 Corinthiens 12:4.†

G0732.def:
ἄρρωστος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., ῥώννυμι), [in LXX: 3Ki.14:5Α, Malachie 1:8 (חָלָה), Sir.7:35 * ;] 
feeble, sickly: Matthieu 14:14, Marc 6:5, 13 16:18, 1 Corinthiens 11:30.†

G0733.def:
ἀρσενοκοίτης, -ου, ὁ
(ἄρσην, κοιτή), 
a sodomite: 1 Corinthiens 6:9, 1 Timothée 1:10.†

G0735.def:
Ἄρτεμις, -ιδος, ἡ 
Artemis, an Asiatic goddess, to be disting. from the Gk. goddess of the same name: Actes 19:24, 27-28

G0736.def:
ἀρτέμων, -ωνος (Rec. -ονος), ὁ 
(ἀρτάω, to fasten to), 
a fore-sail or top-sail: Actes 27:40 (see DB, ext., 366b, 399a; MM, see word).†

G0737.def:
ἄρτι 
adv., [in LXX: Dan LXX 9:22 10:11 (עַתָּה), al. ;] 
adv., 
of coincidence, denoting strictly present time, as contrasted with past or future, just, just now, this moment: Matthieu 3:15 9:18 26:53, Jean 13:7, Galates 4:20, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:6 (see Lft., Notes, 44; Milligan, in l), Apocalypse 12:10; opposite to past time, Jean 9:19, 25 13:33, 1 Corinthiens 16:7, Galates 1:9-10; to future, Jean 13:37 16:12, 31, 1 Corinthiens 13:12, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:7, 1 Pierre 1:6 1:8; ἄχρι τῆς ἅ. ὥρας, 1 Corinthiens 4:11; ἕως ἄ., Matthieu 11:12, Jean 2:10 5:17 16:24, 1 Corinthiens 4:13 8:7 15:6, 1 Jean 2:9; ἀπ᾽ ἄ., see: ἀπάρτι (see Rutherford, NPhr., 70 f; MM, see word).†
SYN.: νῦν, now, "the objective, immediate present; ἤδη, now, already, " the subjective present, with a suggested reference to some other time or to some expectation". (Thayer, 75.)

G0739.def:
ἄρτιος, -α, -ον 
fitted, complete: 2 Timothée 3:17 (MM, see word).†

G0740.def:
ἄρτος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for לֶחֶם ;] 
bread, a loaf: Matthieu 4:3, 4 Marc 3:20, al.; ἄρτοι τ. προθέσεως, bread of the setting forth, i.e. the shewbread. Metaphorical, ὁ ἄ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. ζωῆς, ref. to Christ, Jean 6:33, 35; in general, food: Matthieu 6:11, al.; ἄ. φαγεῖν (Heb. אֲכֹל לֶחֶם), to eat (MM, see word), Lu 14:1, al.

G0741.def:
ἀρτύω 
[in Sm.: Cantique des cantiques 8:2 * ;] 
__1. to arrange, make ready (Hom.). 
__2. Of food (as in comic writers), to season (MM, see word): Marc 9:50, Luc 14:34, Colossiens 4:6.†

G0743.def:
ἀρχ-άγγελος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄρχι-, ἄγγελος), 
archangel, a chief angel: 1 Thessaloniciens 4:16, Ju 9 (Cremer, 24; MM, see word).†

G0744.def:
ἀρχαῖος, -αία, -αῖον
(ἀρχή), [in LXX chiefly for קֶדֶם ;] 
original, ancient: Matthieu 5:21, 33, Luc 9:8, 19, Actes 15:7, 21 21:16, 2 Corinthiens 5:17, 2 Pierre 2:5, Apocalypse 12:9 20:2.†
SYN.: παλαιός, old, without the reference to beginning and origin contained in ἀ. The distinction is observed in π. (MM, see word). ἀ. is the antithesis to καινός: παλ. to vέος (see Westc., He., 223; Cremer, 116)

G0745.def:
Ἀρχέλαος, -ου, ὁ 
Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, King of Judma, Samaria and Idumæa: Matthieu 2:22.†

G0746.def:
ἀρχή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX for קֶדֶם, רֹאשׁ, רֹאשׁ, etc. ;] 
__1. beginning, origin; 
__(a) absol., of the beginning of all things: of God as the Eternal, the First Cause, Apocalypse 21:6 (cf. 18); similarly, of Christ, Apocalypse 22:13; of Christ as the uncreated principle, the active cause of creation, Apocalypse 3:14; in his relation to the Church, Colossiens 1:18; ἐν ἀ., Jean 1:1-2; ἀπ᾽ ἀ. (and ἀπ᾽ ἀ. κτισεως), Matthieu 19:4, 8 24:21, Marc 10:6 13:19, Jean 8:44, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:13, 2 Pierre 3:4, 1 Jean 1:1 Jn 2:13-14 Jn 2:24; κατ ἀρχἀς, Hébreux 1:10; 
__(b) relatively: Hébreux 7:3; ἀ. ὠδίνων, Matthieu 24:8, Marc 13:9; τ. σημείων, Jean 2:11; τ. ὑποστάσεως, Hébreux 3:14; τ. λογίων, Hébreux 5:12; ὁ τ. ἀρχῆς τ. Χριστοῦ λόγος, the account of the beginning, the elementary view of Christ, Hébreux 6:1; ἀρχὴν λαμβάνειν, to begin, Hébreux 2:3; ἐξ ἀ., Jean 6:64 16:4; ἀπ᾽ ἀ., Luc 1:2, Jean 15:27, 1 Jean 2:7 Jn 2:24 Jn 3:11, 2Jn.5-6; ἐν ἀ., Actes 11:15 26:4, Philippiens 4:15; τὴν ἀρχήν, adverbially, at all (Hdt., al.; v MM, see word): Jean 8:25. 
__2. an extremity, a corner: Actes 10:11 11:5. 
__3. sovereignty, principality, rule (cf. DB, i, 616 f.): Luc 12:11 20:20, Romains 8:38, 1 Corinthiens 15:24, Éphésiens 1:21 3:10 6:12, Colossiens 1:16 2:10, 15 Tite 3:1, Ju 6 (Cremer, 113).†

G0747.def:
ἀρχηγός, -όν 
[in LXX for רֹאשׁ, נָשִׂיא etc. ;] 
beginning, originating: more freq., as subst.; 
__1. founder, author (Lat. auchor; so some­times in π., see MM, see word; Milligan, NTD, 75): Actes 3:15 (R, mg.), Hébreux 2:10 (R, txt.; but see Westc., in l, and Page, Ac., l.with). 
__2. prince, leader (so in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 153): Actes 3:15 (R, txt.) Actes 5:31, Hébreux 2:10 (cf. R, mg.) 122 (Cremer, 117).†

G0749.def:
ἀρχιερεύς, -έως, ὁ, 
[in LXX for כּ'' הָרֹאשׁ,כּ'' הַגָּדוֹל ,כּהֵן ;] 
__1. high-priest: Marc 2:26 14:47, al.; of Christ: Hébreux 2:17 3:1, al. 
__2. In pl., chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families: Matthieu 2:4, Marc 8:31, al. (Cremer, 294; DCG, i, 297f.; MM, see word).

G0750.def:
ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ 
[in Sm.: 4Ki.3:4 * ;] 
found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, see word); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, 1 Pierre 5:4.†

G0752.def:
ἀρχισυνάγωγος, -ου, ὁ
(συναγωγή), 
ruler of a synagogue, an administrative officer, supervising the worship (הַכְּנֵםֶת רֹאשׁ): Marc 5:22, 35-36 5:38 Luc 8:49 13:14, Actes 13:15 18:8, 17 (Inscr., see MM, see word; cf. also DB, ext., 101).†

G0753.def:
ἀρχι-τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ
(τέκτων), [in LXX: Ésaïe 3:3 (חָרָשׁ) Sir.38:27. 2Ma.2:29 * ;] 
a master-builder, architect: 1 Corinthiens 3:10 (in π. of building contractors, MM, see word).†

G0754.def:
ἀρχι-τελώνης, -ου, ὁ 
a chief tax-collector, chief publican: Luc 19:2.†

G0755.def:
ἀρχι-τρίκλινος, -ου, ὁ
(τρί-κλινος or -ον, a room with three couches) 
the superintendent of a banquet, whose duty it was to arrange the tables and food (DB, ii, 253): Jean 2:8-9.†

G0757.def:
ἄρχω 
[in LXX for חָלַל, מָשַׁל, etc. ;] 
__1. to begin. 
__2. to rule (see DCG, ii, 538b.): with genitive, Marc 10:42, Romains 15:12. Mid., to begin: before ἀπό, Matthieu 16:21 20:8, Luc 14:18 23:5 24:27, 47, Jean 8:9, Actes 1:22 8:35 10:37, 1 Pierre 4:17; with inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Marc 1:45 2:23 5:17, Luc 3:8, al. (see M, Proverbes 14:1-35 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, see word)

G0758.def:
ἄρχων, -οντος, ὁ
(present ptcp. of ἄρχω), [in LXX for נָשִׂיא., רֹאשׁ, שַׂר, etc. ;] 
a ruler, chief: Jesus, Apocalypse 1:5; rulers of nations, Matthieu 20:25, Actes 4:26 7:35; magistrates, Actes 23:5, Romains 13:3; judges, Luc 12:58, Actes 7:27, 35 16:19; members of the Sanhedrin, Luc 14:1 23:13, 35 24:20, Jean 3:1 7:26, 48 12:42, Actes 3:17 4:5, 8 13:27 14:5; rulers of synagogues, Matthieu 9:18, 23, Luc 8:41 18:18; οἱ ἄ. τ. αἰῶνος τούτου, 1 Corinthiens 2:6-8; of the devil: ἄ. τῶν δαιμονίων, Matthieu 9:34 12:24, Marc 3:22, Luc 11:15; ὁ ἄ. τοῦ κόσμου, Jean 12:31 14:30 16:11; ἄ. τ. ἐξουσίας τ. ἀέρος, Éphésiens 2:2 (MM, see word; DB, iii, 838; Ext., 99 f; DCG, ii, 419; DCG, see word Archon).†

G0759.def:
ἄρωμα, -τος, τό 
[in LXX for בֶּשֶׂם ;] 
spice: Marc 16:1, Luc 23:56 24:1, Jean 19:40.†

G0760.def:
Ἀσάφ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָסַף), [H609]
Asaph, an obvious error for Ἀσά, found in the best texts, and adopted by LTTr. and WH, R, mg.: Matthieu 1:7-8.†

G0761.def:
ἀ-σάλευτος, -ον
(σαλεύω), [in LXX: Exode 13:16, Deutéronome 6:8 11:18 (טוֹפָפָה)* ;] 
unmoved, immovable: Actes 27:41; metaphorically, Hébreux 12:28.†

G0762.def:
ἄ-σβεστος, -ον
(σβέννυμι), [in LXX for נָפַח לֹא, Job 20:26 א3 A (ἄκαυστον, א2 B)* ;] 
unquenched, unquenchable: πῦρ, Matthieu 3:12, Marc 9:43, Luc 3:17.†

G0763.def:
ἀσέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פֶּשַׁע, רֶשַׁע, etc. ;] 
ungodliness, impiety: Romains 1:18 11:26, 2 Timothée 2:16, Tite 2:12; ἔργα ἀσεβείας, ungodly deeds, Ju 15; ἐπιθυηίαι τ. ἀσεβειῶν, desires for ungodly things or deeds, Ju 18 (DB, iv, 532; Cremer, 523; MM, see word).†

G0764.def:
ἀσεβέω, -ῶ
(ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פָּשַׁע, רָשַׁע ;] 
to be ungodly, act profanely: 2 Pierre 2:6; with cogn. accusative (MM, see word), Ju 15.†

G0765.def:
ἀσεβής, -ές
(σέβω, to reverence), [in LXX chiefly for רָשַׁע ;] 
un­godly, impious: Romains 4:5 5:6, 1 Timothée 1:9, 1 Pierre 4:18, 2 Pierre 2:5-6 3:7, Ju 4 15.†

G0766.def:
ἀσέλγεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσελγής, licentious; see MM, see word), [in LXX: Wis.14:26, 3Ma.2:26 * ;] 
licentiousness, wantonness, excess: Marc 7:22, Romains 13:13, 2 Corinthiens 12:21, Galates 5:19 (Lft., in l), Éphésiens 4:19, 1 Pierre 4:3, 2 Pierre 2:2 2:7 2:18, Ju 4.†
SYN.: ἀσωτία, profligacy, prodigality (see Tr., Syn., § xvi; DB, iii, 46).

G0767.def:
ἄσημος, -ον
(σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: Genèse 30:42 (עָטַף), Job 42:11, 3Ma.1:3 * ;] 
without mark (in π. of an uncircumcised boy: Deiss., BS, 153; MM, see word). Metaphorical (MM, see word), unknown, obscure: litotes, οὐκ ἄ (Eur., al.), πόλις, Actes 21:39.†

G0768.def:
Ἀσήρ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָשֵׁר), 
Asher: Luc 2:36, Apocalypse 7:6.†

G0769G.def:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל, etc. ;] 
weakness, frailty, sickness: Luc 13:11-12, Jean 11:4, Actes 28:9, Romains 6:19 8:26, 2 Corinthiens 11:30 13:4, Galates 4:13 (MM, see word), Hébreux 5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jean 5:5, 1 Corinthiens 2:3 15:43, 2 Corinthiens 12:9; pl., Matthieu 8:17, Luc 5:15 8:2, 2 Corinthiens 12:5 12:9-10, 1 Timothée 5:23, Hébreux 4:15.†
SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a)

G0769H.def:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל, etc. ;] 
weakness, frailty, sickness: Luc 13:11-12, Jean 11:4, Actes 28:9, Romains 6:19 8:26, 2 Corinthiens 11:30 13:4, Galates 4:13 (MM, see word), Hébreux 5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jean 5:5, 1 Corinthiens 2:3 15:43, 2 Corinthiens 12:9; pl., Matthieu 8:17, Luc 5:15 8:2, 2 Corinthiens 12:5 12:9-10, 1 Timothée 5:23, Hébreux 4:15.†
SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a)

G0770G.def:
ἀσθενέω, -ῶ
( ἀσθενής) [in LXX chiefly for כָּשַׁל ;] 
to be weak, feeble: Actes 20:35, Romains 8:3, 2 Corinthiens 11:21 12:10 13:4 13:9; with dative, πίστει (Cremer, 527), Romains 4:19 14:1; same implied, Romains 14:2, 21, 1 Corinthiens 8:11-12, 2 Corinthiens 11:29; εἰς, 2 Corinthiens 13:3. Specif., of bodily debility, to be sick: Matthieu 25:36, 39, Luc 4:40, Jean 4:46 5:3, 7 5:13 11:1-3, 6 Actes 9:37, Philippiens 2:26-27, 2 Timothée 4:20, Jacques 5:14; οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, the sick: Matthieu 10:8 (MM, see word), Marc 6:56, Luc 9:2, Actes 19:12.†

G0770H.def:
ἀσθενέω, -ῶ
( ἀσθενής) [in LXX chiefly for כָּשַׁל ;] 
to be weak, feeble: Actes 20:35, Romains 8:3, 2 Corinthiens 11:21 12:10 13:4 13:9; with dative, πίστει (Cremer, 527), Romains 4:19 14:1; same implied, Romains 14:2, 21, 1 Corinthiens 8:11-12, 2 Corinthiens 11:29; εἰς, 2 Corinthiens 13:3. Specif., of bodily debility, to be sick: Matthieu 25:36, 39, Luc 4:40, Jean 4:46 5:3, 7 5:13 11:1-3, 6 Actes 9:37, Philippiens 2:26-27, 2 Timothée 4:20, Jacques 5:14; οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, the sick: Matthieu 10:8 (MM, see word), Marc 6:56, Luc 9:2, Actes 19:12.†

G0771.def:
ἀσθένημα, -τος, τό
(ἀσθενής), 
an infirmity (MM, see word): Romains 15:1.†

G0772G.def:
ἀσθενής -ές
(ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי, etc. ;] 
without strength, weak, feeble: 1 Corinthiens 1:27 4:10 12:22, 2 Corinthiens 10:10, Galates 4:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:14, Hébreux 7:18, 1 Pierre 3:7. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: 1 Corinthiens 1:25; of bodily debility, sick, sickly: Matthieu 25:39 (Rec.) Matthieu 25:43-44, Luc 9:2 (Rec.) Luc 10:9, Actes 4:9 5:15-16 In moral and spiritual sense (MM, see word; Cremer, 526), Matthieu 26:41, Marc 14:38, Romains 5:6, 1 Corinthiens 8:7 8:9-10 9:22 11:30.†

G0772H.def:
ἀσθενής -ές
(ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי, etc. ;] 
without strength, weak, feeble: 1 Corinthiens 1:27 4:10 12:22, 2 Corinthiens 10:10, Galates 4:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:14, Hébreux 7:18, 1 Pierre 3:7. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: 1 Corinthiens 1:25; of bodily debility, sick, sickly: Matthieu 25:39 (Rec.) Matthieu 25:43-44, Luc 9:2 (Rec.) Luc 10:9, Actes 4:9 5:15-16 In moral and spiritual sense (MM, see word; Cremer, 526), Matthieu 26:41, Marc 14:38, Romains 5:6, 1 Corinthiens 8:7 8:9-10 9:22 11:30.†

G0773.def:
Ἀσία, -ας, ἡ 
Asia, the Roman province: Actes 2:9 6:9 16:6 19:1, 10 19:22, 26 (M, Pr., 73), Actes 19:27 Actes 20:4, 16 20:18 21:27 24:18 27:2, Romains 16:5, 1 Corinthiens 16:19, 2 Corinthiens 1:8, 2 Timothée 1:15, 1 Pierre 1:1, Apocalypse 1:4.†

G0774.def:
Ἀσιαός, -ή, -όν 
Asian, of Asia, Asiatic; as subst., ὁ (οἱ) Ἀ.: Actes 20:4.†

G0775.def:
Ἀσιάρχης, -ου, ὁ 
an Asiarch, one of ten officers elected by the various cities in the province of Asia whose duty it was to celebrate at their own charges the public games and festivals: Actes 19:31 (Strab., Inscr.; DB, see word).†

G0776.def:
ἀσιτία, -ας, ἡ 
(ἄσιτος), 
fasting, abstinence from food: Actes 27:21.† 
SYN.: νηστεία (MM, ut infr.)

G0777.def:
ἄσιτος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., σῖτος) 
fasting, without eating (cf. MM, see word): Actes 27:33.†

G0778.def:
ἀσκέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: 2Ma.15:4 * ;] 
__1. to adorn (poët.). 
__2. to practise, exercise (Hdt., Xen.). 
__3. to endeavour (Xen., al.): with inf., Actes 24:16.†

G0779.def:
ἀσκός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX for חֵמֶת, נֹאד, נֶבֶל ;] 
a leather bottle, wine-skin: Matthieu 9:17, Marc 2:22, Luc 5:37-38.†

G0780.def:
ἀσμένως 
adv. (ἥδομαι, to be glad), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:12 2Mac 10:33, 3Ma.3:15 3Mac 5:21 * ;] 
gladly: Actes 21:17.†

G0781.def:
ἄ-σοθος, -ον 
[in LXX: Proverbes 9:8 א2 Α * ;] 
unwise, foolish: Éphésiens 5:15.†

G0782.def:
ἀσπάζομαι depon., 
[in LXX: Eze.18:7, Juges 18:15 (שָׁלוֹם שָׁאַל), Esther 5:2, 1Ma.7:29, al. ;] 
to welcome, greet, salute: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 5:47, Marc 9:15, Actes 21:7, al.; id. before ἐν φιλήματι, Romains 16:16, 1 Corinthiens 16:20, 2 Corinthiens 13:12, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:26, 1 Pierre 5:14; τ. ἐκκλησίαν (Deiss., BS, 257), Actes 18:22; as term. tech. for conveying greetings at the end of a letter (MM, see word), used by an amanuensis (Milligan, NTD, 23), Romains 16:22 (on the aoristic Pres., here and elsewhere, see M, Pr., 119; Bl., § 56, 4); κατήντησαν . . . ἀσπασάμενοι (on this constr., see El., § 58, 4; M, Pr., 132, 238), Actes 25:13 (cf. ἀπ-ἀπ-ασπάζομαι).†

G0783.def:
ἀσπασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἀσπάζομαι), 
a salutation (so always in RV), greeting: oral, Matthieu 23:7, Marc 12:38, Luc 1:29, 41 1:44 11:43 20:46; written, 1 Corinthiens 16:21, Colossiens 4:18, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:17.†

G0784.def:
ἄ-σπιλος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., σπῖλος) [in Sm.: Job 15:15 (LXX, καθαρός)* ;] 
spotless, unstained: 1 Pierre 1:19; metaphorically, 1 Timothée 6:14, Jacques 1:27, 2 Pierre 3:14 (for exx., see MM, see word).†
SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄμωμος

G0785.def:
ἀσπίς, -ίδος, ἡ 
[in LXX for פֶּתֶן, etc. ;] 
an asp: Romains 3:13.†

G0786.def:
ἄσπονδος, -ον
(σπονδή, a libation); 
__1. without truce (Thuc.). 
__2. admitting of no truce, implacable (Dem., al.): 2 Timothée 3:3.†

G0787.def:
ἀσσάριον, -ον, τό
(diminutive of Lat. as), 
an assarion, a farthing, one-tenth of a drachma: Matthieu 10:29, Luc 12:6 (MM, see word; DB, iii, 428; DCG, ii, 200).†

G0788.def:
ἆσσον (Rec., after Vg., Ἄσσον), 
adv. (compar. of ἄγχι, near), 
nearer: Actes 27:13 (RV, close in shore; see B1., § 11, 3; 44, 3; poets, Ion, and late prose).†

G0789.def:
Ἄσσος, -ου
(also Ἀσσός, -οῦ), ή 
Assos, a city on the E. coast of Asia Minor: Actes 20:13-14 (see: ἆσσον).†

G0790.def:
ἀστατέω, -ῶ
(ἄστατος, unstable), [in Aq.: Ésaïe 58:7 (LXX, ἄστεγος)* ;] 
to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, see word): 1 Corinthiens 4:11 †

G0791.def:
ἀστεῖος, -ον
(ἄστυ, a city), [in LXX: Exode 2:2 (טוֹב), Nombres 22:32 (οὐκ ἀ. יָרַט), Juges 3:17 (בָּרִיא), Jdth.11:23, Dan LXX, Sus 1:7, 2Ma.6:23 * ;] 
__1. of the town. 
__2. (Like Lat. urbanus), 
__(a) courteous, 
__(b) elegant (in π., of clothing, MM, see word), comely, fair (as in Ex, l.with), Hébreux 11:23, Actes 7:20.†

G0792.def:
ἀστήρ, -έρος, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב ;] 
a star: Matthieu 2:2, 7-10 :, Marc 13:25, 1 Corinthiens 15:41, Apocalypse 6:13 8:10-12 9:1 12:1, 4; metaphorically, ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνός Apocalypse 2:28 22:16; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches, Apocalypse 1:16, 20 2:1 3:1 (cf. ἄστρον, and see DCG, ii, 674 f.; MM, see word).†

G0794.def:
ἄστοργος, -ον
(στοργή, family affection, love of kindred, see: ἀγάπη) 
without natural affection: Romains 1:31, 2 Timothée 3:3 (MM, see word).†

G0795.def:
ἀστοχέω, -ῶ
(στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Sir.7:19 8:9 * ;] 
to miss the mark, fail: with genitive, 1 Timothée 1:6 (so in π., MM, see word); before περί, 1 Timothée 6:21, 2 Timothée 2:18.†

G0796.def:
ἀστραπή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX for בָּרָק ;] 
lightning: Matthieu 24:27 28:3, Luc 10:18 17:24; pl., Apocalypse 4:5 8:5 11:19 16:18; of a lamp, shining brightness, Luc 11:36.†

G0797.def:
ἀστράπτω 
[in LXX for בָּרָק ;] 
to lighten, flash forth: Luc 17:24 24:4 (MM, see word).†

G0798.def:
ἄστρον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב ;] 
__(a) mostly in pl. (as in cl.), the stars: Luc 21:25, Actes 27:20, Hébreux 11:12; 
__(b) in sing. (Xen., al.), only of some noted star; the symbol or image of a star, Actes 7:43 (cf. ἀστήρ, and see MM, see word).†
